title: Intelligence Explosion Microeconomics
subtitle: MIRI technical report 2013-1
pitch: Yudkowsky's long attempt to turn the intelligence explosion into an empirical question: what are the returns when a mind reinvests in making itself smarter?

chapters.g: The key question: when a system spends effort making itself smarter, does each step get easier or harder?
What evolution, the human brain, human history and computing tell us about those returns.
How this connects to the earlier FOOM debate with Robin Hanson.
A list of empirical questions that would settle the matter, as a research agenda.

ideas: The intelligence explosion is an empirical question about returns.
History gives clues but not answers.
We should try to measure these returns before it is too late.

args.a: Returns on cognitive reinvestment are likely high enough for a fast takeoff.
args.c: Christiano agreed with the central thesis but expected a slower, more continuous takeoff.

questions: Has 2026 data on AI building AI given us the measurements Yudkowsky asked for?

quiz.q: What is the central question of the report?
quiz.w: Does getting smarter make getting smarter easier?
